# TJ Mascots — full content for LLMs

> https://tjmascots.com — the unofficial fan map of every Trader Joe's store hidden animal "mascot" across the U.S.
> Each mascot is treated as a real in-store character (never a toy/plush/doll).
> Generated 2026-06-28T22:56:07.486Z. 352 mascots.
> Open data — please attribute "TJ Mascots fan project (tjmascots.com)" if you publish derivative works.


## AL

### Billy the Black bear
- Store: Birmingham (#737) — Birmingham, AL
- Address: 205 Summit Blvd, Suite 100, Birmingham, AL, 35243
- About: Billy the Black Bear watches over Trader Joe's Birmingham, Alabama on Summit Blvd — a black bear cub with a brown muzzle and tan paws, perched on a green dome in front of the store's painted skyline mural.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/billy-birmingham-737

## AR

### Lil' Rocky the Rock
- Store: Little Rock (#756) — Little Rock, AR
- Address: 11500 Financial Centre Pky, Little Rock, AR, 72211
- About: Lil' Rocky is the resident plush rock at Trader Joe's Little Rock, Arkansas — a perfect punny tribute to the city. A cheerful gray rock with a wild tuft of white hair, posed here on a watermelon-themed display with his Trader Joe's name tag.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/lil-rocky-little-rock-756
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/163.jpg

### Brioche and Toasty the Toast slices (x2)
- Store: El Cerrito (#108) — El Cerrito, CA
- Address: 225 El Cerrito Plaza, El Cerrito, CA, 94530

Spotters: Brioche is still out there somewhere — please snap a photo of Toasty's buddy and submit it!

### Bruce the Shark
- Store: Riverside Dr North (#49) — Sherman Oaks, CA
- Address: 14119 Riverside Dr, Sherman Oaks, CA, 91423
- About: Store 49, 14119 Riverside Dr. Bruce — gray-striped shark, the original Sherman Oaks Trader Joe's mascot. Spotted in an Easter basket with bunny ears (this store dresses him up for holidays). Bruce has held court on the north side of Riverside Drive since long before TJ's #267 opened directly across the street with — of all things — a raccoon. He maintains an icy silence on the matter. Crew members report he has not once acknowledged that the South Side store exists, even when asked directly. Asked once whether he had a comment on Rudy, Bruce reportedly drifted away mid-question.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/bruce-riverside-dr-north-49
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/223.jpg

### Unnamed Cat

Grover returns from vacation.’), complete with a cartoon of him in a Hawaiian shirt and suitcase. The store has been open since around 2004.

### Isla the Channel Islands Fox
- Store: Goleta (#110) — Goleta, CA
- Address: 5767 Calle Real, Goleta, CA, 93117
- About: Isla is the current mascot at Trader Joe's Goleta — a Channel Islands fox, named for the Channel Islands National Park visible from the Santa Barbara coast. The Channel Islands fox is endemic to the islands offshore and an iconic Southern California species. Caught here with her TJ crew member badge in front of a colorful orange-and-purple painted backdrop. Replaced Wally the Walrus (now retired).
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/isla-goleta-110

### Leo the Lion
- Store: Tarzana (#264) — Tarzana, CA
- Address: 18700 Ventura Blvd, Tarzana, CA, 91356
- About: Leo the Lion presides over Trader Joe’s Tarzana on Ventura Blvd — a tan-and-cream lion with a thick golden mane and a TJ badge clearly reading ‘LEO — Crew Member.’ The choice of a lion is no accident: Tarzana itself is named after Tarzan. Author Edgar Rice Burroughs bought a 540-acre ranch in the southern San Fernando Valley in 1919 and named it ‘Tarzana Ranch’ after his famous jungle-hero character. When the surrounding community was officially recognized in 1930, it kept the name. The Tarzan novels are set in the African jungle, so lions are baked into the town’s namesake DNA. The shopping center the store sits in is even called ‘Safari Walk’ — doubling down on the theme.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/leo-tarzana-264
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/466.jpg

### Ocho the Octopus
- Store: North Hollywood (#252) — North Hollywood, CA
- Address: 6130 Laurel Canyon Bl, Suite 100, North Hollywood, CA, 91606
- About: An octopus in landlocked North Hollywood is itself a small surprise — but the name is a quiet nod to area history. In October 1887, J.B. Lankershim and eight other developers organized the Lankershim Ranch Land and Water Company, the syndicate whose 12,000-acre land purchase became modern North Hollywood and the surrounding San Fernando Valley. Ocho (Spanish for 'eight') brings the same number of arms to the job — which the crew swears is genuinely useful for restocking. Photo submitted by David G.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/ocho-north-hollywood-252
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/469.jpg

### Oliver the Bruin
- Store: Los Angeles (#234) — Los Angeles, CA
- Address: 1000 Glendon Ave, Los Angeles, CA, 90024
- About: Oliver the Bruin lives at Trader Joe’s Los Angeles in Westwood, on Glendon Ave — directly next door to UCLA. The choice is no accident: ‘Bruin’ is the universal nickname for UCLA’s sports teams. The word itself has a long history. ‘Bruin’ is a term for a bear, originating from Middle Dutch ‘bruun’ (‘brown’), and became the proper name of the bear character in medieval European fables, most famously in the Reynard the Fox cycle (12th–13th century). It’s long been used as a synonym for a brown bear in English literature, and as a sports-team mascot — UCLA, the Boston Bruins, Brown University, and many more.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/oliver-los-angeles-234
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/453.jpg

### Theodore, Shirley & Jiffy the Squirrels
- Store: Northridge (#312) — Northridge, CA
- Address: 9224 Reseda Blvd, Northridge, CA, 91325
- About: A whole crew of squirrels at Trader Joe’s Northridge on Reseda Blvd — left to right: Theodore, Shirley, and Jiffy. All three are gray-and-cream with TJ crew badges, two of them clutching acorns. The choice is hyper-local: Northridge is the home of Cal State Northridge (CSUN), whose campus is famously overrun with eastern fox squirrels. They’re bold to the point of legend — known to chase students for lunches, ambush picnics, and stand their ground on the quad. The TJ versions are the friendly translation: instead of mugging you for your sandwich, they’ll point you toward the free-sample station.

### Barnacle Billy the Pirate
- Store: Orange (#524) — Orange, CT
- Address: 560 Boston Post Rd, Orange, CT, 06477
- About: Barnacle Billy holds court at Trader Joe's Orange, Connecticut on the Boston Post Road — decked out in full pirate regalia: tricorn hat with skull-and-crossbones, eye patch, red-and-white striped shirt, sword, and a green parrot on his shoulder. The pirate theme is no accident — just down the road in neighboring Milford sits Charles Island, a tiny tidal island famous for its Captain Kidd buried-treasure legend. In 1699, the Scottish pirate Captain William Kidd allegedly buried iron chests of gold and gems there (and supposedly cursed the ground), making this stretch of the Connecticut coastline pirate country in local lore.

### Monty the Manatee
- Store: Naples (#762) — Naples, FL
- Address: 10600 Tamiami Trail N, Naples, FL, 34108
- About: Monty the Manatee glides above Trader Joe's Naples on the Tamiami Trail in southwest Florida — caught here resting on the produce shelf among autumn maple leaves with his Trader Joe's name tag. The species is a perfect Naples local: real Florida manatees (Trichechus manatus latirostris) — Florida's official state marine mammal — graze in the warm Gulf coastal waters and inland rivers all around Collier County, especially during winter when they congregate in warmer spring-fed waterways. Naples-area manatee hotspots include the Faka Union River and Manatee Park up in Fort Myers, and they're a beloved symbol of southwest Florida wildlife — currently listed as threatened, so locals know to slow their boats in manatee zones.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/monty-naples-762
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/424.jpg

### Steeb the Yeti
- Store: Brookline (#501) — Brookline, MA
- Address: 1317 Beacon St, Brookline, MA, 02446
- About: Steeb the Yeti reigns over Trader Joe's Brookline on Beacon Street, Massachusetts — swinging cheerfully in his red scarf in front of a mural of the Green Line trolley (the 'C' branch of which literally runs right down Beacon Street). Yeti sightings around Boston are a real local legend: during the historic 2014–2015 winter — the snowiest in Boston's recorded history, with 110+ inches piled up — a mysterious figure in a full yeti costume started appearing all over town, posing in snowdrifts and shoveling out cars. The 'Boston Yeti' became a folk hero of that brutal winter, racking up viral photos and a beloved social-media following. Steeb feels like the friendly grocery-store cousin of that legend, smiling out from his Beacon St swing through every New England snowstorm.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/steeb-brookline-501
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/419.jpg

### Walter the Blue Whale
- Store: Boston (#566) — Boston, MA
- Address: 44 Thomson Place, Boston, MA, 02210
- About: Walter the Blue Whale lives at Trader Joe’s Boston Seaport on Thomson Place — a perfect mascot for the location, since the store sits right on Boston’s harbor in the maritime Seaport district. Boston Harbor is a major whale-watching launch point: trips out to Stellwagen Bank National Marine Sanctuary regularly spot humpbacks, finbacks, minkes, and the occasional endangered North Atlantic right whale. Walter himself is a stout dark-blue whale with a lighter blue belly, his TJ badge reading ‘WALTER — Crew Member,’ caught here resting atop a row of spice jars.

### Bill the Goat
- Store: Annapolis (#650) — Annapolis, MD
- Address: 160 F Jennifer Rd, Ste F, Annapolis, MD, 21401
- About: Bill the Goat at Trader Joe’s Annapolis on Jennifer Road — named (almost certainly) for ‘Bill the Goat,’ the official mascot of the United States Naval Academy just down the road. The Navy goat tradition dates back to 1893, when sailors brought a live goat from the USS New York to the Army-Navy football game and Navy won; the goat became the academy’s mascot, and every Navy mascot since (currently around Bill XXXVII) has carried the name. Caught here in full Hawaiian-vacation mode — white fluffy coat, floppy yellow ears, draped in a multicolored flower lei.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/bill-annapolis-650
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/450.jpg

### Lucky & Maple the Chickens
- Store: Maple Grove (#713) — Maple Grove, MN
- Address: 12105 Elm Creek Blvd N, Maple Grove, MN, 55369
- About: Two hens hold court at the Maple Grove store: Maple and Lucky. Their names are a nod to the town's roots. Maple Grove was named for the dense stands of sugar maples its first residents prized — the Ojibwe and Dakota, and later the homesteaders, tapped those trees for syrup every spring, and one of the largest sugar maples in Hennepin County still stands watch in the old town cemetery. Maple carries that heritage in her name. Before the subdivisions arrived this was farm country, and no farmstead was complete without a flock — so Lucky struts in as the resident good-luck hen, a wink to the harvests that kept those first families going. Together they keep an eye on the spot where the maple groves and the farm fields once met.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/lucky-maple-maple-grove-713
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/MapleLucky_713.jpg

### Maevis and Marvin the Moose (x2)

### Wally the Walleye
- Store: Minnetonka (#714) — Minnetonka, MN
- Address: 11220 Wayzata Blvd, Minnetonka, MN, 55305
- About: Wally the Walleye swims at Trader Joe’s Minnetonka on Wayzata Blvd — about as Minnesota a mascot as you can possibly pick. The walleye (Sander vitreus) is the official state fish of Minnesota and the single most prized game fish in the Land of 10,000 Lakes. Lake Minnetonka itself, just up the road from the store, is one of the state’s busiest walleye-fishing destinations. ‘Wally Walleye’ is a beloved Minnesota cartoon character/mascot used by the DNR and tourism boards for decades — Trader Joe’s tipping the cap to the local lake culture.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/wally-minnetonka-714
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/452.jpg

### Terri the Pterodactyl
- Store: Clifton (#610) — Clifton, NJ
- Address: 259 Allwood Road, Clifton, NJ, 07012
- About: Terri the Terri-dactyl soars above Trader Joe's Clifton, New Jersey on Allwood Road — wings spread wide in her tropical Hawaiian shirt, hanging from the ceiling with her Trader Joe's name tag. The dino theme is a deeper New Jersey deep-cut than you might expect: NJ is the official Dinosaur State, home of the famous Hadrosaurus discovery in Haddonfield in 1858 (the first nearly-complete dinosaur skeleton ever found in North America). And during the Late Cretaceous, this whole stretch of what's now northern Jersey was coastal terrain where pterosaurs really did glide overhead — so Terri the Pterodactyl gracing the Clifton TJ's is a tribute to a long line of local Terri-dactyls who came before her, 70 million years ago.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/terri-clifton-610
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/421.jpg

### Unnamed Quails
- Store: Las Vegas (#98) — Las Vegas, NV
- Address: 5639 Centennial Ctr Blvd, Las Vegas, NV, 89149
- About: A whole covey of quails (the proper collective noun is a ‘covey’ — also acceptable: a ‘bevy’) lives at Trader Joe’s Las Vegas in Centennial Hills, on the northwest edge of the valley. The species fits the area perfectly: Gambel’s quail (Callipepla gambelii) is the iconic native quail of the Mojave Desert and a familiar sight all around suburban Vegas, easily recognized by its black face and the curling ‘teardrop’ plume on its head. They’re ground-foragers that scurry across yards and washes in family flocks, exactly like this little crew.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/unnamed-quails-las-vegas-98
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/451.jpg

### Cafe the Bluebird
- Store: Nashville (#664) — Nashville, TN
- Address: 3909 Hillsboro Pike, Nashville, TN, 37215
- About: Cafe the Bluebird nests at Trader Joe's Nashville on Hillsboro Pike — and the name is no accident. A few blocks south on the very same street sits The Bluebird Cafe, the legendary 90-seat songwriter listening room founded in 1982 that helped launch Garth Brooks and a generation of Nashville singer-songwriters, and that the world got to know via the TV show 'Nashville'. So 'Cafe the Bluebird' at the Hillsboro Pike Trader Joe's is the most local of local tributes — a quiet little blue-and-rust songbird tucked into a twig nest, just up the road from one of the most famous rooms in American music.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/cafe-nashville-664
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/436.jpg

- Store: Germantown (#738) — Germantown, TN

Caught here in her green-and-red Christmas knit sweater with her TJ ‘PEPPER — Crew Member’ badge, surrounded by her three puggles (the proper term for platypus pups). Posed for a holiday family portrait under a ‘With Your Festive Goodies’ chalkboard.
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/pepper-east-vancouver-272
- Photo: https://tjmascots.com/photos/030.jpg

### Sox the Monkey
- Store: Vancouver (#136) — Vancouver, WA
- Address: 305 SE Chkalov Dr, Vancouver, WA, 98683
- About: Store 136. Sox the Monkey swings around the Vancouver, WA Trader Joe's — named for the sock-like markings on his paws. (Often spelled 'Socks', but the store's chalkboard spells it 'Sox'.)
- Page: https://tjmascots.com/mascot/sox-vancouver-136

### Unnamed Squirrel
- Store: Spokane (#164) — Spokane, WA
- Address: 5520 N Division St, Spokane, WA, 99208
- About: The resident mascot at Trader Joe's Spokane on North Division — a brown furry crew member spotted peeking out from behind a Trader Joe's display sign. We don't know his name or what species he is yet — if you shop here, please tell us!
